A reactionary is a person who believes that society has already changed too much in the wrong direction — and who actively wants to reverse those changes and return to an older way of life or an older political and social order.

The key word here is reverse. Not just stop. Reverse.
The Simplest Way to See It

Think of political views on a straight line:

Progressive → Liberal → Conservative → Reactionary

  • A progressive wants society to change quickly toward new ideas.
  • A liberal wants gradual, forward change.
  • A conservative is broadly happy with how things currently are and wants to preserve them — resist further change.
  • A reactionary thinks things have already gone too far in the wrong direction and wants to pull society backward — to restore something from the past.

So while a conservative says "let's keep things as they are," a reactionary says "things have already gone wrong — we need to go back."

Imagine a country that, over the past 50 years, has:

  • Given women the right to vote
  • Abolished the monarchy
  • Separated church and state

A conservative might say: "Okay, these changes happened. I'm not thrilled, but let's not change anything further."

A reactionary says: "These changes were mistakes. We need to undo them and restore what we had before."

The reactionary isn't resisting future change — they're fighting to reverse past change.
The Political Origins of the Word

The concept was born out of 18th and 19th century European politics. When the French Revolution happened, it tore down the monarchy, the aristocracy, and the Church's political power. Those who wanted to restore the old royal and aristocratic order — to undo what the revolution had done — came to be called reactionaries. They were, quite literally, reacting against the revolution.

Since then, the word has been used broadly across history and countries: anyone who wants to drag society back to a previous era, rather than move it forward.
Why It's Almost Always an Insult

People almost never call themselves a reactionary. It is most commonly used by others — especially those on the left or center of politics — as a criticism, implying that the person's views are:

  • Backward — belonging to a past era
  • Regressive — going in the wrong direction
  • Out of touch — not reflecting how the world works today

Calling someone a reactionary is essentially saying: "Your ideas belong in the past, not the present."

That said, in some corners of modern politics — particularly online — a small number of people have reclaimed the term and use it proudly, wearing it as a badge of honor to signal that they genuinely do believe modern society has gone wrong and needs to return to older values and structures.
Reactionary vs. Words It's Often Confused With

Conservative — A conservative wants to preserve the status quo (the current state of things). A reactionary wants to reverse it. All reactionaries are in some sense conservative, but not all conservatives are reactionary. A reactionary is, so to speak, a conservative on steroids — one who thinks the clock didn't just stop in the right place, but has already gone too far forward and needs to be wound back.

Radical — A radical wants extreme and fundamental change, but the word alone doesn't specify which direction. A radical can want extreme change toward the future (a far-left revolutionary) or extreme change toward the past (a reactionary). In fact, a reactionary can also be described as a radical — just one whose radicalism points backward rather than forward.

Right-wing — A reactionary is typically right-wing, but not every right-wing person is a reactionary. Right-wing broadly means favoring tradition, order, and hierarchy; a reactionary is a specific type of right-wing thinker who specifically wants to restore a past order.
The Word as an Adjective (A Quick Note)

It's worth knowing: "reactionary" is commonly used as both a noun and an adjective, often in the same discussions.

  • As a noun: "He is a reactionary." (referring to the person)
  • As an adjective: "She holds reactionary views." (describing the views)

Same word, two grammatical roles, used interchangeably in political writing and conversation.

A reactionary is a person who believes modern society has already changed too much for the worse, and who wants to reverse those changes and restore an older political or social order — not merely resist further change, but actively go backward.
